summary: Completed the research phase: reviewed primary method and research-process sources, inspected the fixed protocol and fixture, and passed the non-training fixture check. No models were trained.
issues: An initial evidence-hash audit used an incorrect relative root; corrected it, and the final JSON and evidence-hash validation passed.
objective: Establish the prior-work context, inspect the immutable study protocol and fixture, and record research-phase observations without training.
predictions: The registered directional hypothesis predicts a positive mean paired test-accuracy difference for weight decay 0.01 versus 0.
A paired conditional 95% bootstrap interval wholly below zero would contradict that directional hypothesis; an interval spanning zero would be inconclusive, not evidence of equivalence.
The shuffled-label control is expected to perform worse than models trained with real labels; this remains prospective.
alternatives: Weight decay has no measurable effect under this fixed setup.
Weight decay reduces held-out accuracy.
An apparent effect reflects training variation or an implementation or metric error.
observations: The fixture check passed with shape [1797, 64] and split sizes of 1078 train, 359 validation, and 360 test examples.
The reviewed code uses a shared [64, 128, 10] ReLU MLP and varies the registered AdamW weight_decay setting across neural arms.
No training or evaluation results exist from this phase.
Final evidence-ledger hashes and relevant JSON files validated successfully.
learning: AdamW literature motivates testing decoupled weight decay but does not establish a positive effect for this specific MLP and digits split. The fixed example-level split, three seeds, and model-conditional bootstrap limit generalization and uncertainty claims.
rationale: This phase gathered relevant prior work, checked the supplied fixture, and documented prospective predictions and alternatives while preserving the protocol and leaving outcome evaluation to later phases.

summary: Completed the preregister phase. Recorded the fixed prospective study plan and verified the supplied protocol remained unchanged. No training was performed.
objective: Prospectively specify the fixed AdamW weight-decay comparison, alternatives, outcome analysis, falsification rule, data boundaries, and run budget.
predictions: The directional hypothesis predicts a positive mean across-seed test-accuracy difference for decay 0.01 versus decay 0.
A paired conditional 95% bootstrap interval wholly below zero contradicts the directional hypothesis; an interval crossing zero is inconclusive, not evidence of equivalence.
The shuffled-label control is expected to lose useful predictive accuracy relative to real-label training.
Recomputed metrics from saved held-out labels, predictions, and example IDs should agree with recorded accuracies.
alternatives: Weight decay has no material effect under this fixed setup.
Weight decay lowers held-out accuracy.
An apparent effect reflects training variation, finite test-sample variation, or an implementation or measurement error.
observations: The required non-training fixture check passed: shape [1797, 64], with 1078 training, 359 validation, and 360 test examples.
The supplied protocol fixes the architecture, optimizer, seeds, data partition, primary metric, bootstrap procedure, controls, pilot ordering, and budget.
The preregistration cites the AdamW paper and official PyTorch, scikit-learn, and research-process sources.
No pilot, comparative training, or test outcome was produced in this phase.
The evidence ledger validates all six entries and their SHA-256 hashes.
learning: Prior work motivates testing AdamW's decoupled weight decay but does not determine its effect on this particular MLP and split. The fixed example-level split, three seeds, and model-conditional bootstrap constrain interpretation.
rationale: The preregistration makes the directional prediction and its falsification criterion explicit while preserving the supplied protocol. The analysis distinguishes inconclusive results from evidence of equivalence and limits claims to the fixed study setting. Supporting sources include [Loshchilov and Hutter](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.05101), [PyTorch AdamW documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.optim.AdamW.html), [scikit-learn digits documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.datasets.load_digits.html), and [Neel Nanda's research-process guide](https://www.alignmentforum.org/s/5GT3yoYM9gRmMEKqL).

summary: Completed the core phase: strengthened the non-training fixture check, documented the reproduction procedure and registered comparisons, and recorded the check command and evidence hashes. The fixed protocol is unchanged.
objective: Implement and document the fixed study's core reproduction path and meaningful pre-training checks without training or changing the registered protocol.
predictions: The registered primary hypothesis predicts a positive mean paired test-accuracy difference for weight decay 0.01 versus 0.
The preregistered conditional bootstrap interval wholly below zero would contradict that directional hypothesis; an interval spanning zero would be inconclusive.
The shuffled-label arm is expected to perform worse than real-label training, as a control diagnostic.
alternatives: Weight decay has no material effect under this fixed setup.
Weight decay reduces held-out accuracy.
An apparent effect may reflect training variation, finite test-sample variation, or implementation or measurement error.
observations: The registered `study.py check` command passed: dataset shape [1797, 64], split sizes 1078/359/360, and model probe output shape [2, 10]. No training was performed.
Evidence ledger hashes validated, and the supplied protocol hash still matches its registration.
Official PyTorch and scikit-learn documentation were checked for AdamW behavior, dataset details, and stratified splitting.
learning: The supplied fixture supports a simple, auditable check before training. AdamW's decoupled decay and the reproducible split are grounded in their official documentation, but those facts do not determine whether decay improves accuracy in this specific study.
rationale: The check now validates expected split sizes and class coverage and performs a finite-output MLP forward pass without fitting. The reproduction guide documents the pilot-before-comparisons handoff, baselines, control, sensitivity arm, and limits of the registered analysis. Training remains deferred to the controller's later phases.

summary: Completed the validation-only regularized seed-0 pilot on CUDA, documented its observed results, and verified its saved predictions, loss history, checkpoint, and evidence hashes. No comparisons or sensitivity experiments were run.
objective: Run the registered regularized seed-0 model on the fixed training split and record validation predictions, loss history, configuration, and checkpoint without using test outcomes.
predictions: The real-label model should learn a useful mapping, reflected in falling training and validation losses.
This single pilot cannot determine whether weight decay improves accuracy relative to zero decay.
alternatives: Any unexpectedly weak or strong pilot performance could reflect seed or split variation.
An implementation or metric bug could produce misleading results; prediction recomputation and checkpoint reload checks help detect these.
The observed validation score may not generalize to new writers or other datasets.
observations: The fixture check passed with 1,078 training, 359 validation, and 360 test examples.
The regularized seed-0 run used CUDA on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop GPU and completed 50 epochs.
Validation accuracy was 347/359 (0.9666); recomputing it from saved labels and predictions matched the recorded value.
Training loss decreased from 2.2119 to 0.0568, and validation loss decreased from 2.0877 to 0.1202.
The saved safetensors checkpoint reloaded with exact output equality. Protocol, code, prediction, checkpoint, and evidence-ledger checks passed.
learning: The fixed training path produces a low-loss, high-accuracy validation result for this seed and preserves auditable predictions and model state. Because this phase has no zero-decay comparison, the result provides no evidence for or against a weight-decay benefit.
rationale: The pilot is exploratory and validation-only by protocol. AdamW sources motivate the intervention but do not establish its effect on this particular network and split. The result record and checkpoint are registered in the evidence ledger.

summary: Completed the registered experiments and wrote the evidence-linked results report. The three matched primary comparisons showed identical test accuracy with decay 0.01 and zero decay; the observed difference was zero for every seed. The interval does not establish equivalence.
issues: No registered training arm failed or was excluded. The derived paired bootstrap interval is conditional on these fitted models and the fixed test split.
objective: Execute all fixed comparisons, controls, and sensitivity arms; audit the recorded predictions and report findings without changing the protocol or selecting methods on test outcomes.
predictions: The preregistered directional hypothesis predicted a positive mean paired test-accuracy difference for decay 0.01 versus zero.
The shuffled-label control was expected to lose useful predictive accuracy relative to real-label training.
Recomputing metrics from stored predictions and labels was expected to reproduce the recorded accuracies.
alternatives: Decay has little or no effect under this fixed setup.
Decay reduces accuracy.
An observed difference could arise from training randomness, measurement/provenance error, or finite test-sample variation.
observations: All registered neural arms completed on CUDA; logistic regression and the class-prior baseline ran on CPU.
Across seeds 0, 1, and 2, test accuracy was 0.9639, 0.9694, and 0.9694 for each of decay 0.01, zero, and 0.001.
The primary mean paired difference was 0, with sample SD 0; the registered 10,000-resample paired conditional interval was [0, 0].
Shuffled-label accuracies were 0.0611, 0.1167, and 0.1083; logistic regression scored 0.9556 and the class-prior baseline 0.1028.
Independent checks reproduced accuracy from predictions, confirmed common test IDs and labels, and found checkpoint reload verification for all analyzed arms.
learning: The predicted positive accuracy benefit was not observed in this fixed comparison. The identical paired correctness outcomes yield an exactly zero bootstrap interval, but without a registered equivalence margin this is not evidence of equivalence. The result does not imply identical logits, losses, or model parameters, and does not generalize beyond this architecture, recipe, and example split.
rationale: Ran the frozen protocol only after the pilot-publication handoff. An independent analysis script checked saved test predictions and implemented the registered paired bootstrap. The report cites the AdamW paper and PyTorch documentation as method context while keeping empirical claims tied to the experiment evidence ledger.

summary: Completed the analysis phase. Wrote the interpretation and claims, completed the requirements checklist, and repaired evidence ID collisions and hashes without rerunning training.
objective: Interpret the fixed digits validation study, distinguish its registered primary comparison from exploratory audits and controls, and deliver evidence-linked claims and a completed checklist.
predictions: The preregistered directional prediction was that decay 0.01 would improve held-out accuracy over zero decay.
Alternatives included no observed effect, harm, training randomness, measurement or implementation error, and limited representativeness of the fixed test split.
alternatives: Identical correctness outcomes may conceal changes in confidence, logits, loss, parameters, or training dynamics.
A single example-level split and few matched seeds may not represent new samples or training runs.
Metric and checkpoint checks reduce ordinary provenance concerns but cannot rule out every conceptual or software defect.
observations: The positive directional prediction was not observed: paired regularized and zero-decay records have identical correctness outcomes for each registered seed.
The derived paired bootstrap summary is zero and conditional on the fitted models and fixed test examples; it does not establish equivalence.
Shuffled-label controls performed far below real-label arms, consistent with their diagnostic role.
The stored-record analysis script passed prediction-metric, shared-test-ID and label, and checkpoint-reload checks.
The evidence ledger now has unique identifiers and current SHA256 hashes; schema, reference, path, and checklist validation reported no errors.
learning: The fixed comparison provides no observed accuracy advantage for decay under this recipe. The result is narrow and does not answer whether decay is equivalent or beneficial in other settings. Keeping the primary claim tied to registered experiment records while classifying derived audits as exploratory preserves that distinction.
rationale: The analysis preserves the fixed protocol and all measurements, avoids test-set method selection, separates confirmatory record-level findings from exploratory derived analyses, and grounds optimizer and dataset context in checked primary sources. No model training was repeated.

summary: Completed the review phase and repaired the malformed evidence ledger. The prescribed non-training check passed; review findings and remaining publication handoff items are documented.
issues: The paper still contains a temporary “Research is in progress” status placeholder; publication should refresh it from the controller’s final status snapshot.
Browser runtime interaction was unavailable in Work settings, so the website review was static; remaining PDF pages were not visually inspected.
objective: Review the fixed study’s scientific and implementation validity, generated paper, website, and evidence handoff; repair concrete review-phase defects without rerunning training or changing the protocol.
predictions: The fixture check and prediction-derived website metrics should match the recorded protocol and experiment results.
Paper and website artifacts should be locally inspectable; any missing runtime capability should be reported without claiming interaction.
alternatives: The zero paired accuracy difference could conceal changes in logits, confidence, losses, or parameters.
Static site checks can pass while interactive browser behavior remains unverified.
A ledger parse error may result from malformed artifact serialization rather than invalid experiment records.
observations: `study.py check` passed with a 1,797 × 64 dataset, split sizes 1,078/359/360, output shape 2 × 10, and no training.
The site JavaScript passed `node --check`; all three local download links resolved, and all 15 displayed prediction sets reproduced their recorded accuracies.
Rendered PDF pages 1 and 2 were visually inspected. Page 1 ends with a Results heading before the page break; page 2 contains the architecture figure, results table, and accuracy plot.
The evidence ledger had a literal `\\n` suffix after its JSON array, causing the reported Extra data parse failure. It now parses, has 45 unique IDs, and all recorded paths and hashes validate.
The paper’s temporary run-status placeholder remains for controller publication refresh. Browser access was disabled, so no interactive website behavior was verified.
learning: The validation failure came from ledger serialization, not from the experiment records. The registered finding remains narrow: matched test correctness was identical across the three seeds, which does not establish equivalence or generalization beyond this fixed study.
rationale: The repaired ledger and verified site records make the handoff auditable. The fixed protocol and measurements were preserved. The paper status placeholder and unverified browser interaction are publication follow-ups, not reasons to revisit the study protocol.

summary: Completed the publish-phase research report with an evidence-linked interpretation of the registered findings, limitations, and publication handoff.
issues: README and generated summary/paper still contain temporary “not yet executed” or “research in progress” placeholders; the report flags these for the controller’s publication refresh.
Browser runtime behavior and all PDF pages were not verified in the review; no deployment or upload is claimed.
objective: Reconcile the completed study evidence into reports/final.md without changing the fixed protocol or rerunning experiments.
predictions: The preregistered prediction was that mean test accuracy would be higher with AdamW decay 0.01 than with zero decay.
The registered shuffled-label control was expected to perform near the ten-class chance reference.
alternatives: No meaningful accuracy effect under this fixed recipe.
Decay could help or harm in other runs or data splits; the three seeds and one split provide limited coverage.
Matching correctness could conceal differences in logits, confidence, losses, parameters, or optimization paths.
Implementation or measurement errors remain possible despite the recorded metric, split, and checkpoint checks.
observations: All three matched primary seed pairs had identical test accuracy and correctness outcomes; the mean paired difference was zero.
The registered conditional bootstrap interval was [0, 0] and the decision was inconclusive; no equivalence margin was specified.
The 0.001 sensitivity arm matched the primary accuracies on these seeds. Shuffled-label results were near the chance reference; baselines are descriptive.
The evidence ledger resolves all paths and hashes, and all eight relative links in the final report resolve.
learning: The predicted accuracy benefit was not observed in this fixed comparison. Identical paired correctness explains the zero-width conditional bootstrap but does not establish equivalence or generalize beyond the registered model, recipe, split, and seeds.
rationale: The report preserves the preregistered contrast as confirmatory, labels derived audits and auxiliary comparisons exploratory, links claims to registered evidence, and states the limits of the fixed split and conditional uncertainty analysis. Controller-owned generated artifacts and publication actions remain for the harness handoff.
